chapter.title: Passing parts between stations

cards.body:
Your Slack bot just welcomed a new hire called *name*. Not Dana. The actual word "name".

On the assembly line, any station can grab one labelled part off the item that reaches it, but only if you say exactly which part. In n8n that instruction sits between double curly braces, like **{{ $json.name }}: a note that says "grab the part labelled name."**
cards.simpler: Your Slack bot just welcomed a new hire as *name*. Not Dana. The actual word "name". Think of an assembly line. Each station can pick one labelled part off the item in front of it. But you have to say exactly which part. In n8n, you write that request inside double curly braces. **{{ $json.name }} is a note that says "grab the part labelled name."**

cards.prompt: A form hands n8n this item: name = Dana Okafor, team = Sales. Slack should welcome Dana today, and whoever signs up next week too. What goes in the message box?

whyNot.a: That's a fixed value, not a grab: next week's hire would also be welcomed as Dana.
whyNot.c: That's the label, not the part: without braces, Slack prints the word "name".

cards.reteach: Typed text goes out exactly as typed, every time. Braces tell the station to look at the item that arrived and copy in whatever sits under that label.

cards.title: Grab notes, written in braces
cards.body:
An *expression* is a short instruction inside {{ }} that n8n swaps for a real value just before the station runs. Everything outside the braces goes out exactly as typed.

**$json means "the item that just arrived from the station before this one,"** and the word after the dot is the label you want. Labels must match exactly: *team* and *Team* are two different bins.

You rarely type these yourself. Drag a field from the input panel on the left into a box and n8n writes the expression for you. A preview under the box shows what it will turn into.
cards.simpler: An *expression* is a note inside {{ }}. n8n swaps it for a real value before the station runs. Text outside the braces goes out as typed. **$json means "the item that came from the station before,"** and the word after the dot is the label. Labels must match exactly: *team* and *Team* are different. You rarely type these. Drag a field from the left panel into a box and n8n writes it. A preview shows the result.

cards.title: Dana's welcome, end to end
cards.body: The form catches Dana's signup: name Dana Okafor, team Sales. The Slack message box reads: Welcome, {{ $json.name }}! You're joining {{ $json.team }}. The preview shows "Welcome, Dana Okafor! You're joining Sales." On Thursday Marco signs up for Finance, and the same box, untouched, writes his line instead. **One message, written once, right for everyone who ever fills in the form.**
cards.simpler: The form catches Dana's signup: name Dana Okafor, team Sales. In Slack, the message box says: Welcome, {{ $json.name }}! You're joining {{ $json.team }}. The preview reads "Welcome, Dana Okafor! You're joining Sales." On Thursday, Marco signs up for Finance. Nobody touches the box, and it writes his welcome instead. **One message, written once, right for everyone who ever fills in the form.**

cards.prompt: Your form saves the team answer under the label *team*, all lowercase. You want Slack to say which team each new person joins. Which goes in the message?

whyNot.b: That's a different label, not the one on the part: capital T points at an empty bin, so the team comes out blank.
whyNot.c: That's a fixed value, not a grab: Marco from Finance would be told he joined Sales.

cards.reteach: A station only finds a part if the label matches letter for letter, capitals included. Copy it from the input panel, or drag it in so n8n spells it for you.

cards.title: Reaching further up the belt
cards.body:
You'd think every station can see the whole belt. It can't. $json only sees the item from the station *right before*. Put a Gmail station between the form and Slack, and Slack receives Gmail's receipt: a message ID and little else. Dana's name isn't on it.

So you reach back by station name: **{{ $('Signup Form').item.json.name }} grabs the name from the form, however far back it is.**

The *Edit Fields* node is the tidy-up bench. It renames awkward labels, like *Full name (as on ID)* to *name*, and drops parts you don't need, so later grabs stay short.
cards.simpler: $json only sees the item from the station right before. Put a Gmail station between the form and Slack, and Slack gets Gmail's receipt: a message ID, but no name. You reach back by station name. **{{ $('Signup Form').item.json.name }} grabs the name from the form, however far back it is.** The *Edit Fields* node tidies up. It renames messy labels, like *Full name (as on ID)* to *name*, and drops parts you don't need, so later grabs stay short.

cards.body: Sam built the welcome bot, typed Welcome, $json.name! into the Slack box with no braces, and switched it on. Twelve new hires were greeted, in public, as $json.name. The box was in *Fixed* mode, so n8n sent the words exactly as typed. Before you switch anything on, check that **the preview under the box shows a real name, not code**.

The box was in *Fixed* mode, so n8n sent the words exactly as typed. Before you switch anything on, check that **the preview under the box shows a real name, not code**.

cards.prompt: Your line runs Signup Form, then Gmail sends a thank-you, then Slack posts Welcome, {{ $json.name }}! Slack shows a blank where the name should be. Why?

options.text: Slack can't show names that came from a form.
$json reads Gmail's item, the station right before, and it has no name on it.
Expressions need three curly braces, not two.

whyNot.a: That's blaming the station, not the grab: Slack prints whatever text it's handed.
whyNot.c: That's the wrapping, not the label: two braces is right, the grab just found nothing.

cards.reteach: Each station passes on its own item, not the one it received. After Gmail, the belt carries Gmail's receipt. Name the station you want: {{ $('Signup Form').item.json.name }}.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
In n8n, **anything inside {{ }} is a grab** that copies a labelled part off an item, so one message works for every person. $json grabs from the station right before; to reach further back, name the station.

Tomorrow: how one field decides which of two belts an item rides.
cards.simpler: In n8n, **anything inside {{ }} is a grab**. It copies a labelled part off an item, so one message works for every person. $json grabs from the station right before. To reach further back, name the station. Tomorrow: how one field decides which of two belts an item rides.

cards.body: Open the workflow from chapter 3. Click into the message box, switch it to Expression, and drag one field in from the left panel. Run it once and check the preview shows a real value, not the code.
cards.simpler: Open the workflow from chapter 3. Click into the message box and switch it to Expression. Drag one field in from the left panel. Run it once. Then look at the preview under the box. Make sure **it shows a real value, not the code**.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now take a name from step 1 and put it into a message sent in step 3.
